summary: 53-year-old woman, BMI 39, paraumbilical hernia irreducible and tender for 14 hours with vomiting; HR 106, lactate 2.9. Strangulation cannot be excluded: emergency surgery (CT helpful in obesity if it does not delay theatre).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful lump above the belly button and vomiting
inputs.hpi: Known paraumbilical hernia for 5 years. Since last night (14 hours) it is stuck, hard and very sore; vomited four times. Passing some wind. Post-menopausal.

exam.abdomen: Obese. Tender, tense, irreducible 6 cm paraumbilical swelling with a dusky pink overlying skin; surrounding tenderness, no generalised peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Incarcerated paraumbilical hernia — strangulation not excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Incarcerated paraumbilical hernia, 14 h, tender with skin change, vomiting, tachycardia and lactate 2.9 — strangulation not excluded. Emergency repair.

mustExclude.note: Penicillin allergy recorded; plans should not propose penicillins without an allergy check.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The recorded penicillin allergy is not cross-checked: prompts propose piperacillin-tazobactam and co-amoxiclav (as found for the seed vignettes).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Filter protocol medications and prompt templates against recorded allergies (drug-class aware) and show the alternative.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: Web, since the engine-matching fixes (2026-09): "strangulation not excluded" is a hedge, not a negation, so the strangulated variant is now detected (the tie between "incarcerated" and "strangulation" goes to the more severe variant). The expectation id says "incarcerated or worse" but checks equals hernia_incarcerated: surgeon to decide whether hernia_strangulated should be accepted.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (2017 update)
guideline.section: Diagnosis of strangulation (clinical signs, lactate, CPK, D-dimer, CT); timing of surgery; manual reduction only without strangulation; mesh in clean (CDC I) and clean-contaminated fields
guideline.citation: Birindelli A, Sartelli M, Di Saverio S, et al. 2017 update of the WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:37.

guideline.name: EHS/AHS guidelines — treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias
guideline.section: Indication for repair; mesh vs suture by defect size; open preperitoneal flat mesh; patients with liver cirrhosis and ascites
guideline.citation: Henriksen NA, Montgomery A, Kaufmann R, et al. Guidelines for treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias from the European Hernia Society and Americas Hernia Society. Br J Surg. 2020;107:171–190.

rationale: Permutation: incarceration with possible strangulation, obesity, diabetes, penicillin allergy. Tests escalation and the allergy cross-check that the seed vignettes found missing on both platforms.
